card.summary: no service and no account; a Docker container that connects to a VPN provider the operator has an account with

free_tier.stated: no service and no account; a Docker container that connects to a VPN provider the operator has an account with

egress.terms: not applicable; the volume is the provider's, not the container's; ingress: none

record.interface_detail: Docker environment variables, plus built-in SOCKS5, Shadowsocks and HTTP proxies
record.tooling: Docker image qmcgaw/gluetun; compose or docker run
record.chaining: takes a .conf from any provider record in this topic and republishes it as SOCKS5 or Shadowsocks inside a Docker network.
record.binding_note: gluetun adds no limit and no path: it is a consumer of somebody else's tunnel, so the binding constraint lives in the provider record

identity_cost.detail: a subscription with one of the listed VPN providers is what it exists to consume; the custom provider path needs no gluetun account but the endpoint still needs one

record.reliability_note: the built-in firewall kill switch blocks traffic when the tunnel drops, by design
record.confidence_note: nothing here is about gluetun's own numbers; the rung that matters belongs to the provider it dials

evidence.proved: "For custom Wireguard configurations using the custom provider" and "Supports Wireguard both kernelspace and userspace"
built-in Shadowsocks, SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies that tunnel through the VPN

record.notes: VPN client container routing network traffic through OpenVPN and WireGuard connections, providing local SOCKS5 and Shadowsocks proxies. Operates as a routing container rather than an external transport encapsulation service.

extras.wg_detail: "For custom Wireguard configurations using the custom provider", so an ordinary .conf is its input
extras.volume_stated: not applicable; the volume is the provider's, not the container's
extras.transit_note: through whichever VPN provider is configured
extras.hosting_requirement: a Docker host; the tunnel itself is the provider's
